# Tentative Project Title
<div class="section-divider"></div>

**Exploring the Usage Pattern of CitiBike in NYC**

# Motivation
<div class="section-divider"></div>

By analyzing trip-level data from CitiBike NYC, this project aims to understand  
ridership patterns, including factors influencing:

- ride frequency  
- distance  
- duration  
- start and end station selection  

Insights may help:

- improve bike availability during peak hours  
- optimize station placement  
- enhance overall user experience  

# Intended Final Products
<div class="section-divider"></div>

- An interactive website summarizing key CitiBike usage trends  
- Visualization of ride frequency patterns  
- Seasonal and demographic breakdowns  
- Heat maps showing popular start and end stations  

# Anticipated Data Sources
<div class="section-divider"></div>

Primary dataset:

- CitiBike NYC official trip-level data (CSV)  
  https://citibikenyc.com/system-data  

Additional metadata:

- Station information  
- NYC borough shapefiles (optional)

# Planned Analyses / Visualizations
<div class="section-divider"></div>

- Ride frequency by time of day, season, membership type, gender  
- Spatial distributions of start & end stations  
- Hotspot analysis  
- Potential clustering of ride routes  

# Coding Challenges Anticipated
<div class="section-divider"></div>

- Handling large CSV files (multi-million rows)  
- Combining datasets across months  
- Spatial mapping & coordinate alignment  
- Maintaining site performance with large visual outputs  

# Planned Timeline
<div class="section-divider"></div>

| Week | Tasks |
|------|-------|
| Week 1 | Choose and clean the CitiBike datasets |
| Week 2 | Basic analysis + visualize key trends |
| Week 3 | Build website and check visualizations |
| Week 4 | Write final report + polish website |
